summary: The hydraulic lift theory (Landreau, PLOS ONE 2024) applies to the Step Pyramid of Djoser, NOT the Great Pyramid; it is controversial and criticized by archaeologists.
content: Landreau et al. (PLOS ONE, Aug 2024) proposed a hydraulic lift for the Step Pyramid of Djoser at Saqqara, using the Gisr el-Mudir enclosure as a check dam and the Dry Moat as a water treatment system, with a float in the north shaft raising stones. This applies to the Step Pyramid, NOT the Great Pyramid of Giza. It is controversial: critics note no Egyptologists/archaeologists were directly involved (Julia Budka), Gisr el-Mudir could not hold enough water (Oren Siegel), the proposed lake is not attested in any texts (Kamil Kuraszkiewicz), and Djoser's blocks were much smaller (~300kg) than later pyramids'. The theory is unproven and does not bear on the Great Pyramid's construction.
